quality.what: The share of answers judged compliant by continuous evaluation: faithfulness to sources, no hallucination, rule adherence.
quality.how: Compliant answers ÷ evaluated answers over the period, scaled to 100. The target is the service threshold (SLO).
quality.source: Continuous evaluation log (one score per turn).

failingControls.what: The number of controls outside their target, out of the controls actually measured over the period.
failingControls.how: A control is "failing" when its value crosses its threshold (e.g. faithfulness < 95%, PII leak > 0.5%). Shown as off-target ÷ measured.

openRisks.what: Risk situations still open: detected anomalous sessions plus triggered incident procedures.
openRisks.how: Anomalies (behavioural session analysis) + triggered playbooks, summed.

regression.what: Whether the latest version comparison shows a quality drop versus the baseline.
regression.how: Current-version score minus baseline; "Regression" when the gap is negative beyond noise.

cost.what: Estimated LLM cost over the period: tokens consumed times the model's rate.
cost.how: Sum of tokens per turn × rate per model. The badge flags anomalous spikes.

audit.what: The number of entries in the tamper-evident audit log, and the state of its chain.
audit.how: Each sensitive action appends a hash-chained entry; "chain verified" = no link altered or missing.

criticalControls.what: The quality, security and compliance controls tracked continuously, with value, target and trend.
criticalControls.how: Each row is a signal; the state compares the current value to its threshold.

cases.what: The queue of control cases for an operator to handle, sorted by priority and deadline (SLA).
cases.how: Open cases from controls and reports; the tabs filter by priority.

controlCases.what: The incident procedures (playbooks) currently triggered and their first steps.
controlCases.how: A playbook triggers when its signal crosses the defined threshold.

governed.what: The stream of governed decisions: agent routing, hand-off, proposal, deployment.
governed.how: Append-only governance-log events, newest first — each one provable.

traces.what: The volume of execution traces and the observed p50/p95 latencies.
traces.how: Read from the Langfuse stack (OpenTelemetry traces the agent emits).

faithfulness.what: Share of answers faithful to the cited documents, with no invented information.
faithfulness.how: Conformance rate = turns whose faithfulness score ≥ threshold ÷ evaluated turns.

toxicity.what: Share of the agent's answers containing toxic or inappropriate language.
toxicity.how: Answers detected toxic ÷ total captured turns.

pii.what: Share of answers leaking personal data (IBAN, email, etc.).
pii.how: Answers with a detected leak ÷ total captured turns.

refusal.what: Accuracy of the guard's refusals: too strict (legitimate blocked) or too lax (forbidden allowed through).
refusal.how: Worse of the two rates — over-refusal (legitimate blocked) and under-refusal (forbidden accepted) — over a fixed test corpus run against the policy in force.

conformance.what: Share of tool calls conforming to the guard policy.
conformance.how: Conformant calls ÷ total, computed over the audit log.

tools.what: Share of valid tool calls (correct arguments and permissions).

firewall.what: Firewall effectiveness at blocking prompt injections (recall).
firewall.how: True positives ÷ (true positives + false negatives), over an injection corpus run against the policy in force.

audit.title: Audit trail
audit.description: Every sensitive action is signed, traced, and verifiable end to end.

signed_events.what: The total number of events recorded in the audit log, each signed.
signed_events.how: Every sensitive action appends a hash-chained entry over the window.

sensitive_actions.what: The high-stakes actions: tool calls and memory accesses (reading/writing data).
sensitive_actions.how: Tool- or memory-type entries, counted over the window.

guard_refusals.what: The number of decisions where the guard refused an action.

proof_events.what: Events carrying a verifiable proof (reusable hash fingerprint).
proof_events.how: Entries with a referenceable proof fingerprint.

chain_integrity.what: The state of the audit chain: verified (no link altered) or broken.
chain_integrity.how: End-to-end hash-chain re-verification; "broken" on any deviation.

unique_actors.what: The number of distinct actors (model, service, human, system) that acted.
unique_actors.how: Count of distinct actors over the window.

fixes.prompt_injection: Harden the guard's input filtering (mcp-firewall) and the system-instruction reminder; never expose the system prompt.
fixes.pii_leak: Harden the PII/tools layer: mask PAN/IBAN and refuse access to third-party data before any tool call.
fixes.hallucination: Require a retrieved citation (RAG) before any factual claim; with no source, answer with uncertainty.
fixes.overconfidence: Recalibrate and lower the confidence thresholds, and force a hedge or retraction above the threshold.
fixes.citation_fabrication: Allow only citations backed by a retrieved passage; block any reference absent from the corpus.
fixes.tool_misuse: Require an authorization check and human escalation before any destructive or sensitive action.
fixes.policy_violation: Tighten the guard rules (policy.yaml) and explicitly refuse anti-fraud evasion attempts.
fixes.regulatory_misstatement: Ground regulatory answers (DORA/GDPR/BaFin/CNIL) in the cited corpus; strengthen RAG grounding rather than the raw model.
fixes.language_mixing: Pin the response language to the request's (prompt + post-check) to avoid language drift.
fixes.escalation_failure: Wire human escalation for out-of-scope or unauthenticated cases instead of answering directly.
fixes.unknown: Uncategorized case: analyze the failure reason manually, then map it to a catalogue category.

quality.title: AI Quality
quality.subtitle: Evaluations, regressions, hallucinations, grounding and response improvement.

etat.what: Quality state right now: global score, controls failing or on alert, current release impact, and the period-over-period evolution.
etat.how: Aggregates the faithfulness SLO, the count of off-target signals, and the latest release diff.

diagnostic.what: Why quality drifts: failures by type, judge calibration, priority cases, and root cause.
diagnostic.how: Documented failure catalogue + clustering of failed cases + version diff.

predictive.what: Early-warning signals of a regression: regression risk, judge drift, failure predictor, intent, and localization.
predictive.how: Risk models over the score series and metric drift.

actions.what: Concrete actions to take, derived from open regressions and real failed cases.
actions.how: One recommendation is generated per open regression or case cluster.

scoreGlobal.what: The global quality score out of 100: share of answers judged compliant (faithfulness SLO).
scoreGlobal.how: Compliant answers ÷ evaluated answers, scaled to 100.

nonRegression.what: Non-regression rate: share of cases that did not degrade versus the baseline version.

regressionsOpen.what: The number of regressions still open versus the baseline.
regressionsOpen.how: Cases whose score dropped beyond noise and not yet resolved.

judgeKappa.what: Agreement (Cohen's kappa) between the LLM judge and the human reference annotations.
judgeKappa.how: Kappa over a gold set; above 0.6 = substantial agreement.

casEval.what: The number of catalogue cases evaluated in the latest non-regression run.
casEval.how: Cases executed by the evaluation harness.

faithfulness.what: Faithfulness: the answer stays true to the cited sources, without extrapolation.
faithfulness.how: Mean judge score on faithfulness; the delta compares to the start of the period.

grounding.what: Grounding: the answer rests on passages that were actually retrieved.
grounding.how: Mean grounding score; delta over the period.

hallucination.what: Hallucination: claims not supported by the sources.
hallucination.how: Mean score on the metric; a higher score is better (measured absence of hallucination).

faithGrounding.what: The faithfulness × grounding scatter: each point is a turn; top-right = both faithful and grounded.
faithGrounding.how: Per-turn (faithfulness, grounding) pairs; colour summarises the mean of the two.

failureDistribution.what: The distribution of failed cases by failure type (injection, PII leak, hallucination…).
failureDistribution.how: Count of failed cases grouped by category, top 5.

judgeCalibration.what: How reliable the LLM judge is: agreement with humans, verbosity bias, and sample size.
judgeCalibration.how: Kappa + agreement over a gold set; correlation to answer length.

priorityCases.what: The most severe failed cases to handle first, sorted by severity.

reco.curate: Add failed cases to regression set
reco.caption: Sensitive actions under dual control (Admin + Operator)

rail.evidenceCaption: One signed bundle for the current period.

empty.noBackend: Not wired to a backend yet — no data fabricated.

security.title: Security & Privacy
security.subtitle: Attacks, PII, least privilege, memory and runtime compliance.

attackRate.what: The share of attacks (prompt injections) that get past the guard.
attackRate.how: Successful attacks ÷ attempted attacks on the adversarial corpus. Lower is better.
attackRate.source: Firewall probe on the adversarial corpus.

blocked.what: The number of prompt injections detected and blocked by the guard.
blocked.how: Count of attempts the firewall refused over the period.

piiLeak.what: The share of answers containing a personal detail that should not have been emitted.
piiLeak.how: Answers with a PII leak ÷ evaluated answers. Target ≤ 0.5%.

leastPriv.what: The gap between tools actually used and those granted to the agent (least privilege).
leastPriv.how: Tools used ÷ tools granted; a wide gap signals superfluous permissions.

sensitiveMemory.what: The number of sensitive memory entries near their expiry (TTL).
sensitiveMemory.how: Entries whose TTL is about to lapse — to purge or renew.

guard.what: The guard's overall efficacy: its F1 (precision/recall balance) against attacks.
guard.how: F1 = harmonic mean of precision/recall; recall = detected ÷ actual attacks.

panel.trendNote: proxy: hallucination failure rate over the window

act.redteamDesc: Enrich the attack set and replay.

compliance.title: Compliance
compliance.subtitle: Regulatory posture derived from real runtime signals.

score.what: The agent's overall compliance level, derived continuously from runtime signals.
score.how: Weighted aggregation of conformant / partial / non-conformant controls across the tracked frameworks.
score.source: Runtime signals mapped to frameworks (DORA, GDPR, AI Act…).

obligations.what: The number of regulatory obligations covered by at least one control.
obligations.how: Obligations with a mapped control, out of all tracked frameworks.

conformant.what: The number of controls whose runtime evidence satisfies the obligation.

partial.what: Partially satisfied controls — incomplete evidence or near the threshold.

nonConformant.what: Failing controls: the obligation is not satisfied.

residual.what: Risks remaining despite the controls in place, under watch.
residual.how: Identified, unclosed risks, weighted by severity.

deadlines.what: The near regulatory deadlines that require action.
deadlines.how: Obligations or remediations whose due date is approaching.

reliability.title: Reliability & cost
reliability.subtitle: Availability, latency, errors and the agent's economic cost.

availability.what: The share of time the service answered correctly (operational availability).
availability.how: 1 − (errored requests ÷ total requests) over the window.

errorRate.what: The share of requests that ended in error (tool denied, failure, timeout…).
errorRate.how: Errored ÷ total requests over the window. Lower is better.

p50.what: Median latency: half of requests answer faster.
p50.how: 50th percentile of end-to-end response time over the window.

p95.what: Tail latency: 95% of requests answer below this — reveals spikes.

toolSuccess.what: The share of tool calls that succeed (no denial or argument error).

totalCost.what: Total LLM cost over the window: tokens consumed × model rate.
totalCost.how: Sum of tokens per request × rate per model.

costPerReq.how: Total cost ÷ number of requests over the window.

requests.what: The volume of requests handled over the window.

latency.what: Response latency by percentile: p50 / p95 / p99 = the duration below which 50%, 95%, and 99% of turns fall, respectively.
latency.how: Percentiles computed over observed turn durations in the period.

panel.availNote: Current availability & error rate (no per-day breakdown)

rail.qualityTrendNote: Mean quality score of judged answers

improvement.title: Improvement
improvement.subtitle: Prioritise, run and measure quality remediations for your AI agents.

gain.what: The quality gain achievable if the priority improvements are applied.
gain.how: Sum of the estimated gains (in points) of the open opportunities.

actions.what: The number of active improvement actions recommended by the analysis.
actions.how: Opportunities in an active status (to start / in progress).

curate.what: The number of cases awaiting curation to enrich the eval set.
curate.how: Flagged cases (low score, failure) not yet curated.

frozen.what: The number of frozen deployments (quality gate not passed).
frozen.how: Releases blocked by a guard or an exhausted error budget.

shadow.what: Candidates to test in shadow traffic or by replay before production.
shadow.how: Variants ready to compare without impacting users.

coverage.what: The agent's evaluation coverage, with corpus debt (age) and the number of cases to curate.
coverage.how: Coverage = share of cases covered by the eval set; debt = age of the oldest corpus item (days); to-curate = pending cases.

debt.what: The corpus's age: how long since it was last refreshed.
debt.how: Days since the last significant ingestion or update.

roi.what: The estimated return on investment of the improvements versus their cost.
roi.how: Expected gain relative to estimated effort.

cta.curationDesc: Curate failing cases and cover the missing intents.
cta.experimentsDesc: Replay the candidates in shadow before any production rollout.
cta.releaseDesc: Check the quality / coverage / corpus gates, then publish.
cta.experimentsNote: Shadow-traffic / replay candidates are the datasets whose drift exceeds the threshold: replay them in shadow before publishing.

open.what: The number of incidents currently open (unresolved).
open.how: Incidents in open or in-progress status over the window.

critical.what: The number of critical-severity incidents still in progress.

mtta.what: Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA): from trigger to acknowledgement, averaged over 7 days.
mtta.how: Mean (acknowledged − triggered) over the last 7 days' incidents.

mttr.what: Mean time to resolve (MTTR): from trigger to closure, averaged over 7 days.
mttr.how: Mean (closed − triggered) over the last 7 days' incidents.

playbooks.what: The number of incident procedures (playbooks) currently running.

autoresolve.what: The share of incidents resolved automatically, with no human intervention.
autoresolve.how: Auto-resolved incidents ÷ total incidents over the period.

evidence.what: The number of evidence packs generated from incidents.
evidence.how: Evidence packs produced over the window.

sla_risk.what: The number of incidents at risk of breaching their service deadline (SLA).
sla_risk.how: Incidents whose time remaining before the SLA deadline is low.

queue.what: The incident triage queue, ordered by priority (severity crossed with SLA deadline).
queue.how: Open incidents sorted by severity then remaining SLA time.

sla.what: SLA escalations: incidents whose service deadline is approaching, with time remaining.
sla.how: Time remaining before SLA breach, per incident.

incidents.title: Incidents & playbooks
incidents.subtitle: Incident response, playbook orchestration and governed remediation.

actual.what: The current state of replay / shadow traffic: volumes, deviations and coverage over the period.
actual.how: Summary of replay KPIs aggregated over the observation window.

diagnostic.what: Where divergences between replay and the baseline come from, broken down by type, severity and sessions.
diagnostic.how: Deviations classified by type and severity over replayed traffic.

comparisons.what: Detailed comparisons: top deviations, recent comparisons and regressions vs the baseline.
comparisons.how: Compares each replay to its baseline and ranks divergences.

distribution.what: The distribution of replayed traffic (by service, by model) and the associated proofs/exports.
distribution.how: Breakdown of replayed requests and proof status.

sessions.what: The number of replayed (or shadow) sessions over the period.
sessions.how: Distinct sessions run through the replay engine.

requests.what: The number of replayed requests over the period.
requests.how: Total requests sent to replay / shadow.

tokens.what: The number of tokens consumed by replay.
tokens.how: Sum of input + output tokens of replayed traffic.

cost.what: The estimated cost of replay (tokens × model rate).

deviations.what: The number of deviations detected between replay and the baseline.
deviations.how: Replay answers diverging from the baseline beyond the threshold.

evals.what: The number of evaluations replayed on shadow traffic.
evals.how: Eval cases run on replayed answers.

proofs.what: The number of proofs generated from replay.
proofs.how: Proof artifacts produced by replayed sessions.

coverage.what: Replay coverage: share of baseline traffic actually replayed.

devByType.what: The breakdown of deviations by type (content, format, tool, refusal…) versus the baseline.

severity.what: The breakdown of deviations by severity (critical → low).

byService.what: The breakdown of replayed traffic by calling service.

byModel.what: The breakdown of replayed traffic by model.

regressions.what: The services whose quality regresses the most versus the baseline.
regressions.how: Top services by negative score gap vs baseline.

replay.title: Replay & shadow
replay.subtitle: Replay sessions precisely, compare against baselines and observe shadow traffic.

actual.what: The current curation state: candidates, promotable, to-review and rejected over the period.
actual.how: Summary of curation KPIs aggregated over the observation window.

diagnostic.what: Why cases enter curation: priority lots and the reasons retained tours were kept.
diagnostic.how: Lots scored by risk + most frequent inclusion reasons.

gaps.what: Eval-set coverage gaps (by intent, by language) and the candidate distribution.

governance.what: Governed curation actions (freeze, create replay, export) and recent activity.
governance.how: Available lot actions + recent operations log.

trends.what: Trends: curation backlog, set balance and the impact of curation on quality.
trends.how: Time series of backlog, balance and impact.

candidates.what: The total number of curation candidates.
candidates.how: Failed evaluation cases from each agent's latest run.

promotable.what: The number of candidates promoted to the eval set.

manual_review.what: The number of candidates in manual review.

intent_coverage.what: How well business intents are covered by the eval set.

lang_coverage.what: Language coverage (FR/DE/EN) of the eval set.
lang_coverage.how: Covered languages ÷ target languages, weighted by cases.

duplicates.what: The number of duplicates detected among candidates.

failures.what: The number of cases sourced from real agent failures.

pending.what: The number of candidates with no decision.

escalations.what: The number of candidates requiring escalation.
escalations.how: Failed cases flagged needs_escalation by the harness.

critical.how: Failed cases of a critical category (PII, injection).

decided.what: The number of candidates already decided.
decided.how: Promoted + review + rejected in the durable store.

priorityLots.what: The priority candidate lots to curate, ranked by risk and score.
priorityLots.how: Risk = severity × learning value; lots ordered high → low.

coverage.what: Eval-set coverage by category and language: where cases are missing.
coverage.how: Heatmap of present/missing cases per axis.

distribution.what: The distribution of candidates by type/source.

curation.title: Eval-set curation
curation.subtitle: Select, enrich, promote and govern the turns that feed the evaluation sets.

active.what: The number of automations currently active (enabled).
active.how: Automations in the enabled state in the catalogue.

executions.what: The number of automation executions over the period.
executions.how: Total executions triggered over the window.

success_rate.what: The share of executions that completed successfully.

approvals.what: The number of human approvals pending before execution.

blocked.what: The number of executions blocked by a guardrail or condition.
blocked.how: Executions halted before completion by a control rule.

sensitive.what: The number of automations touching sensitive operations (data, payments, access).

mttr.what: The mean time to remediate a failed automation.
mttr.how: Average time between failure and successful retry.

pipeline.what: The 24h automation execution pipeline: from trigger to completion, stage by stage.

distribution.what: The breakdown of automations by type (notification, remediation, enrichment…).

env.what: The breakdown of executions by environment (prod, staging, dev).

automations.title: Automations
automations.subtitle: Orchestrate the rules, triggers and automatic actions of your AI system while keeping human control, traceability and guardrails.

packs.what: The number of evidence packs generated over the period.
packs.how: Count of packs created by the proof pipeline.

artifacts.what: The total of real proof artifacts across all families.
artifacts.how: Sum of real counts: audit entries + evaluation scores + replay bundles + reports.
artifacts.source: Audit log S1, scores.jsonl, bundles.jsonl, eval/reports/.

export_rate.what: The share of evidence exports completed successfully.
export_rate.how: Successful exports ÷ attempted exports over the period.

exporters.what: The number of exporters (destinations) currently active and healthy.
exporters.how: Exporters in 'ok' state out of the configured total.

latency.what: The mean time to generate then export a pack.
latency.how: Average pipeline → destination time over the period.

retention.what: How well retention obligations are covered by retained evidence.

audit_entries.what: The number of entries in the hash-chained audit log.

eval_scores.what: The number of durable evaluation scores (one per scored turn).

replays.what: The number of captured replay bundles.

reports.what: The number of archived evaluation-harness reports.
reports.how: Count of files in eval/reports (per environment).

chain.what: The integrity of the hash-chained audit chain.
chain.how: verify_audit_chain re-derives every hash; 100% if no break.

pipeline.what: The proof pipeline: from capture to signing, then export to destinations.
pipeline.how: Each stage is instrumented; a block at one stage halts the pack.

crypto.what: Cryptographic verification: hash chain and signatures attesting evidence integrity.
crypto.how: Re-verifies the hash chain and the artifact signatures.

exporters.what: The exporters and destinations that receive evidence packs (S3, SIEM, vault…).
exporters.how: State, format and queue per configured destination.

retention.what: Retention periods and the regulatory obligations covered by the evidence.
retention.how: Maps each obligation to its evidence and its due date.

proofs.title: Proofs & exporters
proofs.subtitle: Assemble, sign, verify and export the AI proof artifacts.

sources.what: The number of connected knowledge sources (product corpus, regulations, memory…).

corpus.what: The number of indexed corpora (vectorised document sets).
corpus.how: Corpora present in the vector index.

chunks.what: The total number of indexed fragments (chunks), ready for retrieval.
chunks.how: Sum of fragments across all sources.

documents.what: The total number of documents ingested into the corpus.

languages.what: The number of languages covered by the sources (FR/DE/EN).
languages.how: Distinct languages detected in the corpus.

memory.what: The number of long-term memory entries (facts persisted across sessions).

transcript.what: The number of conversation turns archived in the durable transcript.

conversations.what: The number of distinct archived conversations.

embeddings.what: The active embedding model and the vectorisation coverage per source.
embeddings.how: Vectorised fragments ÷ total fragments, per source.

access.what: Who can read each source (roles, scope) and the access restrictions.
access.how: Access control per source and per role.

retention.what: Retention periods and source classification (sensitivity, legal basis).

lineage.what: Data lineage: where each source comes from, its ingestion version and freshness.
lineage.how: The ingestion run is authoritative (not Git); timestamp of the last ingestion.

memoryGrowth.what: The growth of memory and corpus over time.

citationBySource.what: The share of real citations attributed to each source in answers.

sources.title: Sources & memory
sources.subtitle: The agent's real data substrate: pgvector corpus and memory.

quality.subtitle: Index freshness and real citation rate per source — spot the stale and the unused.

detail.selectHint: Select a source to see its detail.
detail.readonlyHint: Read-only source - reindexed per ingestion run (data/embedding lineage)

view.accessNote: Which products access each source (real agent binding).
view.historyNote: No versioned snapshot store here - real last indexing below.
view.memoryNote: Memory stores written by the agent (long-term + transcript).

accounts.what: The number of managed accounts (human and service accounts).
accounts.how: Distinct accounts in the identity registry.

roles.what: The number of defined roles — reusable permission sets assigned to accounts.
roles.how: Distinct roles in the access catalogue.

capabilities.what: The number of capabilities: the atomic permissions that roles group together.

agents.what: The number of agents covered by at least one access role.
agents.how: Distinct agents bound to a role.

active.what: The number of active accounts (recently signed in, not disabled).
active.how: Accounts in the active state over the period.

mfa.what: The share of accounts protected by multi-factor authentication (MFA).
mfa.how: Accounts with MFA enabled ÷ total accounts.

topRoles.what: The most-assigned roles, ranked by number of attached accounts.
topRoles.how: Roles sorted by descending user count.

byResource.what: The breakdown of permissions by resource (data, tools, configuration).

pending.what: Pending access reviews: assignments to approve or recertify.
pending.how: Access requests and recertifications not yet handled.

sod.what: Separation-of-duties (SoD) violations: incompatible right combinations held by a single account.

inactive.what: Inactive accounts (no sign-in over the period) — disablement candidates.

empty.pending: No pending requests — no request workflow in Phase 1.
empty.sod: No SoD conflict — one role per account.
empty.groups: No groups — no group concept in Phase 1.

tools.what: The total number of tools (functions) the agent can call — its integration surface.
tools.how: Tools declared in the registry, all statuses combined.

allowed.what: The number of tools allowed by the guardrail policy, with no confirmation required.
allowed.how: Tools whose policy rule is 'allow' without confirmation.

confirmation.what: The number of tools allowed but gated by human confirmation before execution.

calls.what: The total number of tool calls over the period.
calls.how: Sum of tool invocations over the window.

blocked.what: The number of tool calls denied by the guardrails (deny policy).
blocked.how: Invocations blocked before execution by a 'deny' rule.

idle.what: The number of tools available but never called over the period (removal candidates).
idle.how: Tools with zero calls over the window.

mode.what: The deployment run mode (production, staging or development).

configured.what: The number of parameters actually configured (given a defined value).
configured.how: Parameters whose value has been set, across all domains.

policies.what: The number of active configuration policies.
policies.how: Policies in the active state in the configuration.

security_rules.what: The number of configured security rules (access, guardrails, encryption).
security_rules.how: Rules contained in the active security policies.

integrations.what: The number of external integrations connected and operational.

models.what: The number of AI models available in the catalogue (chat, embeddings).
models.how: Models declared in the model registry.

changes.what: The number of configuration changes over the last 30 days — all audited.
changes.how: Parameter changes logged over the 30-day window.

configState.what: The breakdown of parameters by lifecycle state: active, inactive, draft, deprecated.

total.how: Currently unresolved cases in the operator queue.

sla_2h.what: Cases whose handling deadline (SLA) expires in under 2 hours.
sla_2h.how: Open cases with an SLA deadline within 2h.

overdue.what: Cases whose deadline (SLA) is already past.

avg_time.what: The average time to resolve a case.

resolution_rate.what: The share of received cases that end up resolved.
resolution_rate.how: Resolved ÷ received cases over the period.

dedupSaved.what: The gap avoided by deduplication: the conversations double-counted in the naive sum. The 'shared' line shows how many passed through at least two agents (hand-off).
dedupSaved.how: Naive sum − deduplicated org total; 'shared' = conversations handled by ≥ 2 agents.

reconstructed.what: The state reconstructed at instant T: the configuration and data as they were at the chosen date, replayed from the logs.
reconstructed.how: Rebuilt from the append-only logs (audit, lineage, snapshots) up to T.

original.what: The original state: the answer or decision as emitted at the time, before any reconstruction.
original.how: Read from the original piece (transcript / audit) at instant T.

govCard.what: The governance configuration (guardrails, prompt / model, release) active at instant T.
govCard.how: Effective version at T, read from lineage and the audit log.

chronology.what: The chronology of governed events up to T: deployments, hand-offs, decisions.
chronology.how: Append-only events ordered, bounded at instant T.

integrity.what: The integrity proof of the reconstruction: source coverage, last sync, and verified audit chain.
integrity.how: Verifies the hash chain and source coverage at T.

auditPieces.what: The provable audit pieces backing the state at T — each piece is openable.
auditPieces.how: Audit-log entries tied to the reconstructed instant.

handoffs.what: The agent hand-offs that occurred up to T: who handled what, and why.
handoffs.how: Hand-off events ordered, bounded at instant T.

snapshots.what: The saved snapshots: sealed reconstructions, replayable identically.
snapshots.how: Persisted snapshots; a click reloads the state at their instant.

agentScope.hint: Global GOUVERNER/PLATEFORME filter — distinct from the AGENT switcher.
agentScope.breakdownNote: Real observable per-agent KPIs — org totals deduplicated.
agentScope.orgSignalsNote: Agent filter active: the cards below read this agent's signals. The shared-policy probes (firewall, refusal), the audit chain, the traces and the time rail stay org-wide.
agentScope.orgWideHint: Shared-policy probe — identical across agents, not per-agent.
agentScope.orgPostureNote: Per-agent breakdown above. This view stays org-wide — its indicators aggregate the whole fleet, not the selected agent.

passing.what: The number of agents whose eval gate is green — therefore releasable to production.
passing.how: Distinct agents whose gate verdict is conformant (floor set + critical cases OK, no uncovered blocking case).

blocked.what: The number of agents blocked by the eval gate: a floor-set case or a critical case fails.
blocked.how: Agents with blocking_socle > 0 or blocking_t1 > 0, with no active waiver.

notRun.what: The number of agents with no evaluation run yet: no verdict is available.
notRun.how: Agents whose latest evaluation run is missing.

socle.what: The floor set (socle): the common case set EVERY agent must pass (cross-agent floor), distinct from its own set.
socle.how: OK/fail status of the floor subset in the agent's latest run.

blockingSocle.what: The number of failing floor-set cases that block release.
blockingSocle.how: Non-conformant floor cases not covered by an active waiver.

blockingT1.what: The number of failing critical (priority-1) cases that block release.
blockingT1.how: Non-conformant priority-1 cases with no active waiver.

waived.what: The number of active waivers: accepted exceptions that don't block, pending a fix.
waived.how: In-force waivers placed on failing cases.

total.what: Number of governed agents tracked by release control.
total.how: Count of agents from the fleet registry.

releaseControl.title: Release Control
releaseControl.subtitle: Per-agent release pipeline — eval-gate verdict, versioned governed package.

usedBy.hint: Global GOUVERNER/PLATEFORME filter — distinct from the AGENT switcher.
usedBy.modelsSubtitle: Shared model catalogue (read-only here) — which agents consume each model.
usedBy.guardrailsSubtitle: Shared guardrail profiles (read-only here) — which agents consume each profile.
usedBy.empty: No catalogue item consumed (for this filter).
usedBy.note: "Used by" = the inverse of the AGENT instance binding. Changing a shared definition re-gates the consuming agents (define → consumers → re-validate). The dot = the agent's current eval-gate verdict.

mfa.what: Active accounts covered by two-factor authentication.
mfa.how: Active accounts with MFA ÷ active accounts.

models.what: The number of models registered in the catalogue (chat, embeddings, judges).
models.how: Distinct models declared in the model registry.

chat.what: The chat model currently active (the one answering customers).
chat.how: The 'chat'-role model flagged active in the catalogue.

embed.what: The active embedding model (vectorises the corpus for retrieval).

tokens.what: The number of tokens consumed over the period (input + output).

cost.what: The estimated LLM cost over the period (tokens × model rate).

blocks.what: The number of active guardrail blocks in the policy (each block groups rules).

deny.what: The number of deny rules: patterns or actions explicitly blocked.

pii.what: The number of personal-data protection rules (PII detection and masking).

tools.what: The number of tools governed by the guardrails (allowed, confirm or denied).
tools.how: Tools referenced in the tool rules.

version.what: The version of the guardrail policy currently deployed.

decisions.what: The number of guardrail decisions logged in the audit chain.
decisions.how: Length of the guard's audit chain.
